content.text:
The planner hint predicted absence, but investigation shows a robust Vendor indemnity that meets or exceeds our preferred position:

- **p0047–p0051**: Kubient defends, indemnifies and holds harmless Customer *and* its officers/directors/agents/employees against third-party Claims arising out of (i) the Services, (ii) the Auction Platform, (iii) Creative, (iv) Kubient's breach of any rep/warranty, and (v) acts/omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors.
- **IP coverage confirmed**: the "Services"/"Auction Platform" prongs are unqualified, and prong (iv) picks up Kubient's express non-infringement warranty at **p0033**.
- **p0053–p0055**: standard procedure (prompt notice with no forfeiture for delay, indemnitor control, no liability-admitting settlement without consent, cooperation at indemnitor's cost).
- **p0027**: indemnification is expressly carved out of the consequential-damages waiver, and there is **no monetary cap anywhere** — better than the fallback's 3× super-cap.

The only divergence from preferred is that Customer's indemnity (p0052) is reciprocal rather than narrowed to Customer content and breach of law. Given the Vendor indemnity is uncapped and broader than our model language, reopening this symmetric clause would be disproportionate and risks unravelling a favourable bargain — so no redline.

input.quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
input.rationale: The planner flagged this rule as likely absent, but Section 10(a) (p0047-p0051) contains a broad Vendor indemnity in AP's favour that satisfies the preferred position. Kubient defends, indemnifies and holds harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents and employees against third-party Claims arising out of (i) the Services, (ii) the Auction Platform, (iii) Creative placed via the Auction Platform, (iv) Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and (v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors. IP infringement is covered twice over: the "Services" and "Auction Platform" prongs are unqualified and contain no IP carve-out, and prong (iv) captures Kubient's express warranty at p0033 that the Service and deliverables "do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party." Prong (v) also reaches Kubient's negligence and wilful misconduct, and p0035 plus prong (iv) cover data-security failures by Kubient. Section 11 (p0053-p0055) supplies standard procedure: prompt written notice with express confirmation that delay does not relieve the indemnifying party, indemnitor control of defence and settlement subject to no admission of liability against the indemnified party without consent, and cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost. Commercially, the indemnity is stronger than our fallback: p0027 expressly carves indemnification out of the mutual consequential-damages waiver, and a search for any aggregate liability cap returned nothing, so Kubient's indemnity is uncapped rather than limited to 3x annual fees. The only divergence from the preferred position is that Customer's indemnity at p0052 is reciprocal in structure (unauthorised use of the Services/Platform, breach of rep or warranty, Content and Properties, and acts or omissions of Customer) rather than narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. That mirrors Kubient's own prongs, and Customer already accepts sole responsibility for Content and Properties at p0025 and warrants their non-infringement at p0043-p0044, so the allocation is symmetric. Given the Vendor-side indemnity is uncapped and broader than our model language, reopening this balanced clause to trim Customer's side would be disproportionate and risks unravelling a bargain that favours us. No redline proposed.
